activities.anchor: positions on taxes, crime, immigration and family correlate
activities.caption: file each principle under its family
activities.name: idBundlesSort

config.prompt: The big three by their staples — file each principle:

items.label: natural rights held against the state, not gifts from it
government by consent, rule of law, tolerance of difference
organic society — hierarchy and authority as natural and functional
class analysis — society divided by relation to production

config.why: Each family is a coherent package: the positions correlate because they flow from deeper commitments — equality against liberty, universalism against particularism, reason against tradition.

activities.caption: pair each liberal thinker with the move they made
activities.name: idThinkersMatch

config.prompt: The liberalism shelf — pair each thinker with their contribution:

pairs.right: individuals hold rights prior to government; when it breaches the trust, the people may replace it
pointed the logic at gender — liberalism generating feminism from its own premises
the harm principle — power justified only to prevent harm to others
negative liberty (freedom from interference) versus positive liberty (freedom to)
the minimal state — redistributive taxation 'on a par with forced labor'

config.why: The classical-versus-social split is a dispute about what freedom is — and both answers are liberal answers; only the freedom concept moved.

activities.caption: true or false — the conservative shelf
activities.name: idConservJudge

statements.s: Conservatism parses human imperfection psychologically, morally and intellectually.
statements.why: We crave belonging, we are capable of cruelty, and our reason is fallible — the three parsed starting points.

statements.s: Oakeshott described politics as 'keeping afloat' on a well-found ship, attending to symptoms rather than sailing for utopias.
statements.why: Rationalism in Politics (1962) gave the twentieth-century version of the temperament.

statements.s: One-Nation conservatism's 'noblesse oblige' is an obligation of the rich to the poor.
statements.why: Disraeli took the organic metaphor seriously — reform conserves order by extending stake.

statements.s: The New Right was a single strand, purely neoliberal.
statements.why: It fused neoliberalism (Hayek, Friedman — roll back the state) with neoconservatism (strengthen authority, family and nation) — an internal and real tension.

activities.anchor: formal rights mean little where property concentrates
activities.caption: order the socialist arc, thinker by thinker
activities.name: idSocialistOrder

config.prompt: The socialist arc, in order of appearance — assemble it:
items: Marx and Engels: historical materialism and surplus value — revolution and the state that 'withers away'
Rosa Luxemburg: mass spontaneity, not a vanguard committee
Sidney and Beatrice Webb: the Fabian road — research, permeation, the ballot box
Anthony Crosland: nationalisation was a means — the end is equality and social justice
Anthony Giddens: the Third Way — social investment, rights balanced with responsibilities
config.why: Revolutionary versus evolutionary, ownership versus welfare — the split that cost lives in 1917–1921 arguments and ended with Blair rewriting Clause IV.

config.q: Socialism, communism, the USSR — are they all the same thing?
choices: yes — socialism is just the polite name for Soviet rule
no — socialism is the family; communism its revolutionary-Marxist wing, social democracy its reformist wing
config.why: The Soviet experiment was one branch's governance — as authoritarian as it was — and other socialists, Luxemburg among them from the left, predicted and denounced that authoritarianism early.

activities.anchor: Its record is the twentieth century's catastrophe
activities.caption: drag the divider — the two 'beyond' answers
activities.name: idOthersCompare

config.prompt: Drag the divider — fascism and anarchism, stated precisely:

before.label: fascism totalises
before.text: The nation (or race) as an organic unity above the individual: ultra-nationalism, the leader principle, struggle as the engine of renewal — anti-liberal and anti-Marxist at once.

after.label: anarchism dissolves
after.text: 'No one — no state': both Marxist and liberal states concentrate coercion; voluntary association, mutual aid and federated communes can coordinate what states claim only they can.

config.why: The contrast sharpens the big three: liberalism individualises, socialism socialises, conservatism historicises — fascism totalises, anarchism dissolves.

activities.anchor: Four regularities from the research literature
activities.caption: one line of this ideology-behaviour briefing is wrong
activities.name: idBehaviourSpot

config.prompt: One line of this student's briefing on how ideologies behave is wrong — click it:
lines: Issue positions correlate because they flow from deeper commitments — the bundle is the ideology.
Converse showed the correlation is real but thinner among low-information voters — ideology is partly expertise.
Ideologies are fixed systems whose freeze-frame definitions never go stale.
The internal fights — Rawls vs Nozick, Luxemburg vs Crosland — are where the interesting arguments live.
Knowing a position on one axis moderately predicts the rest of the bundle, and the 'big sort' tightens it further.
config.correction: They evolve: conservatism adapts to what it conserves, liberalism absorbed its own socialist critique — Freeden's morphology is the update mechanism.
config.why: Steel-manning is the practical skill: caricature makes you unable to predict what an ideology's supporters will do next.
